sections.overview: The Common Scoter breeds across northern Eurasia and winters mainly at sea along European coasts, with farther east Asian wintering also reported.
sections.identification: The male is mostly black with a conspicuous yellow-orange knob on the bill; the female is brown.
sections.habitat: It nests near freshwater lakes and rivers in northern regions, then uses coastal and offshore marine waters outside the breeding season.
sections.diet: It dives for benthic prey, especially marine bivalves; crustaceans, gastropods and small fish can also be eaten.
sections.behavior: Outside the breeding season it gathers in large flocks on marine waters and dives to feed.
sections.reproduction: It breeds in solitary pairs near freshwater; species-specific nest and clutch details are omitted here because the consulted sources differ in coverage.
sections.ecology: Along parts of the French coast, it is a regular wintering sea duck and may occur alongside the Velvet Scoter (*Melanitta fusca*).
sections.conservation: Globally, it is Least Concern, but the UK's small breeding population is Red-listed and contracted between national surveys.
